question: Which private-equity rivals are most active in our sectors?
html:
Residential home services is the busiest field. National consolidators and four sponsors buying in Pennsylvania and New Jersey compete directly with Punctual Pros for add-ons. Commercial electrical, legal IT and lab distribution each have one or two sponsor-backed rivals, and none has a direct copy of BSP's position yet (PE competitive landscape).

Rivals by sector

BSP portfolio companyMost active rivalsRead
Punctual ProsApex/Alpine, Wrench/LGP, TurnPoint/OMERS, Redwood/Altas, Any Hour/Knox Lane, T3/Riverside; locally Sila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy/HL Bowman (Gridiron), Ally (Watchtower), Northwinds (TruArc)Most crowded; national consolidators set add-on pricing
CETKohlberg (RESA Power, Loenbro, CLEAResult); Huron (Criticore, Albireo)Mostly outside the six-state footprint
FrontlineAlpine's Evergreen, EagleTree/Integreon, BVNo direct sponsor-backed copy yet
Thomas ScientificCalibre ScientificMain bidder for U.S. add-ons

Home services detail

  • Apex did 46 add-ons in 2023 and 60 in 2025 (home-services case studies).
  • The scaled companies (Wrench, Apex, Redwood, Legacy) borrow at S+425–475 with loans marked at par. They can keep funding deals (competitor filings).
  • The next tier is weaker. TurnPoint, Any Hour and Len the Plumber have moved to part-PIK interest, with marks of 89–94 (competitor filings).
  • Horizon Services is lender-owned by 2026 (home-services case studies). Heartland's debt matures Dec 15, 2026 (competitor filings).
  • These two regional rivals look more likely to sell assets than to bid hard for add-ons (est.).

Electrical and strategic buyers

  • PE now accounts for most electrical-contractor M&A since 2023 (PE competitive landscape).
  • IES is a public strategic buyer, not a sponsor. It has no net debt and an 11.4% operating margin, so it can pay strategic prices for New England contractors (competitor filings).
  • The rivals to watch are Albireo, through its Upstate NY expansion, and Kohlberg's energy-efficiency cluster.

Fund-level peers

  • The closest thesis peers are MidOcean, CIVC, Trilantic North America, Palladium, Vesterra/Comvest and Bertram (PE competitive landscape).
  • BSP's fund is about $335M. Rivals such as Trivest VII ($950M), Bertram V ($1.5B) and Gridiron V ($2.1B) are much larger.
  • BSP therefore depends on co-invest and operating credibility to compete.

Data gaps

  • There is no rival data here for Bully Pulpit International or Fair Harbor. Deal logs for strategic-communications agencies and consumer apparel would answer this.
  • Several fund sizes are unknown, including Gryphon VI, Trilantic VII and Palladium VI.
  • Add-on counts are not given for most rivals beyond Apex. Deal-count data would allow a true ranking of activity.

Next actions

  • Punctual Pros: Build a proprietary outreach list of shops under $3M EBITDA in Central PA/NJ. Lean on Authority Brands territory rights and brand conversion rather than joining auctions.
  • Distressed rivals: Track Horizon and Heartland for asset sales around and after Dec 15, 2026.
  • CET: Speed up New England add-ons before the Kohlberg and Huron companies enter the region. Monitor Albireo's Upstate NY moves.
  • Frontline: Lock in law-firm MSP and legal billing add-ons before a generalist MSP consolidator builds a legal vertical.
